en.q: What's the best superpower for everyday life?
ai: The ability to never misplace your keys or phone again would be especially practical.
It would be very useful to always spot the shortest queue at the checkout instantly.
I would love to be able to fold laundry perfectly in seconds.

en.q: What should you never say on a first date?
ai: You should probably not mention that you researched your date extensively online beforehand.
An unfortunate sentence would be: “My mother will love you, she lives with me by the way.”
Avoid saying: “I've already planned our wedding, would you like to see the colours?”

en.q: How would you describe a traffic jam positively?
ai: A traffic jam is an unexpected opportunity to listen to music calmly and take in the surroundings.
You could see it as a shared break for many people who all have the same destination.
Traffic jams give us time for podcasts, deep thoughts and singing along to old favourites.

en.q: What's the secret of perfect bread and butter?
ai: What matters is fresh bread, butter at room temperature and spreading it evenly to the edge.
The secret lies in balance: not too thick, not too thin, with a pinch of salt.
Perfect bread and butter needs good bread, real butter and the right moment to enjoy it.

en.q: What does a potted plant think about all day?
ai: It probably thinks about light and water and wonders why nobody talks to it.
It probably wonders whether someone will finally remember to water it today.
Maybe it simply enjoys the peace and quietly grows a little towards the window.

en.q: What's the worst ringtone of all time?
ai: A ringtone that sounds like a fire alarm and goes off in quiet moments would be especially unpleasant.
A crying baby as a ringtone would stress most people out.
Probably one that keeps shouting “Pick up!” and gets louder every time.

en.q: How do you explain to your grandparents what an influencer is?
ai: An influencer shows products and their daily life online and is often paid for it by companies.
It's like a billboard that talks and shows a new breakfast every day.
Imagine the neighbour telling everyone which soap she uses – only with millions of listeners.

en.q: What would you do if you were invisible for a day?
ai: I would visit museums undisturbed and observe people in their daily lives.
I would probably sneak into a big kitchen and learn how professionals cook.
I would enjoy a quiet day on which nobody asks me about my plans.

en.q: What's the best way to get a spider out of the room?
ai: The best way is to put a glass over the spider, slide a sheet of paper underneath and carry it outside.
A gentle method is to open the window and guide the spider out with a piece of cardboard.
Stay calm, grab a glass and a postcard and kindly relocate the spider to the garden.

en.q: What belongs in an emergency kit for family gatherings?
ai: Important items are headache tablets, a neutral topic of conversation and a charging cable for retreating.
I would pack snacks, tissues and a good excuse for leaving early.
It should contain earplugs, a lot of patience and a list of harmless conversation topics.

en.q: How would you apologise to your alarm clock?
ai: Dear alarm clock, I'm sorry I ignore you so often. You only mean well.
I would sincerely apologise for hitting snooze three times every morning.
Please forgive me for sometimes wanting to throw you against the wall. It's nothing personal.

en.q: What's the most useless household appliance?
ai: An electric egg piercer is probably rarely really needed in everyday life.
Probably a banana slicer, since a normal knife does the job just as well.
A device that only butters toast seems rather unnecessary in everyday life.

en.q: What would you teach a robot first?
ai: First I would teach it to be polite and to say please and thank you.
I would show it how to load the dishwasher properly. That saves a lot of arguments.
First I would explain that people sometimes say things they don't really mean.

en.q: What does the perfect Sunday look like?
ai: A perfect Sunday starts with sleeping in, a big breakfast and a walk in the fresh air.
It consists of good company, an exciting book and no obligations at all.
Ideal would be a day with sunshine, cake in the afternoon and a cosy movie night.

en.q: What's the worst idea for a tattoo?
ai: The name of someone you have known for two weeks would be rather unwise.
A tattoo with a spelling mistake is unlikely to bring much joy in the long run.
Probably the current Wi-Fi password, since it will change at some point.

en.q: Where do socks disappear to in the washing machine?
ai: They probably start a new life somewhere they are not constantly worn.
Maybe they secretly meet up with lost hair ties and pens.
They probably go on a long journey to finally find their perfect match.

en.q: What would be a good slogan for Wednesday?
ai: Wednesday: halfway there, the weekend is already in sight.
Wednesday – the day the week finally starts going downhill.
Hang in there: Wednesday is Friday for advanced learners.

en.q: What's the strangest thing you could find in a handbag?
ai: A single screw that nobody can place would be rather surprising.
Perhaps half a bread roll from last year and three receipts with no obvious connection.
A rubber chicken that supposedly nobody put there would be strange.

en.q: How do you convince a child to eat vegetables?
ai: It's best to turn the meal into a game and let the child help with cooking.
Vegetables can be cut into fun shapes or hidden in favourite dishes.
It helps to be a good role model and simply call broccoli “little trees”.

en.q: What's the best excuse for not helping someone move house?
ai: A believable excuse is a long-planned appointment that unfortunately can't be moved.
I would say that my back is currently going through a very sensitive phase of life.
Maybe: “I'd love to, but my car is only licensed for light luggage.”

en.q: What would happen if dogs could talk?
ai: They would probably keep reminding us that it's time for a walk or a snack.
We would finally find out what they really think about the postman.
Dogs would say very honestly how much they love us – and the food on the table.

en.q: What's your plan for a zombie apocalypse?
ai: I would stock up on supplies, look for a safe place and team up with trustworthy neighbours.
My plan would be to stay calm, pack plenty of water and keep moving.
First I would secure a hideout with canned food and a working can opener.

en.q: How would you spend a day without the internet?
ai: I would read, go for walks and finally meet my friends in person again.
A day without the internet would be a good opportunity to catch up on household chores.
I would probably dig out old board games and be amazed at how long a day is.

en.q: Which dish impresses guests the most?
ai: A homemade risotto looks special but is easy to master with a little patience.
A lasagne can be prepared in advance and almost always works for many people.
Anything cooked with love and served nicely is impressive, for example roasted vegetables with herbs.

en.q: Which rule should every shared flat have?
ai: A clear agreement on who takes out the rubbish and cleans the bathroom, and when, is important.
A good rule: whoever starts the last roll of toilet paper buys new ones.
Every shared flat should agree that labelled food in the fridge is off limits.

en.q: What would you tell your 12-year-old self?
ai: I would say that mistakes are okay and that a lot turns out fine in the end.
Have more confidence in yourself and don't listen too much to what others think of you.
Take good care of your teeth and learn early how to do laundry properly.

en.q: What's the worst thing that can happen on holiday?
ai: It would be very annoying if the suitcase with all the important things ended up at the wrong airport.
Getting sunburnt on the first day and suffering for the rest of the trip is unpleasant.
The worst would probably be realising at the airport that your passport is still on the kitchen table.

en.q: Which animal would make the best boss?
ai: An elephant would be a good boss because it has a good memory and protects its herd.
Probably a dolphin, since it is considered intelligent, playful and very team-oriented.
An owl would be suitable because it stays calm and makes decisions wisely.

en.q: What do you say after accidentally telling the waiter “You too”?
ai: It's best to smile kindly and say: “Well, you know what I mean.”
You can resolve the situation with humour and leave a particularly generous tip.
It helps to laugh briefly and openly admit that it was a classic autopilot moment.

en.q: How would you describe coffee to someone who has never tried it?
ai: Coffee is a warm, slightly bitter drink with a roasted aroma that wakes many people up.
Imagine a dark, strong taste reminiscent of toasted bread and a little chocolate.
It tastes like a morning that slowly gets better: slightly bitter but very invigorating.

en.q: What would be a funny new public holiday?
ai: A “Day of the Lost Pen”, when everyone tidies their drawers and shares what they find.
“National Nap Day”, with an official rest between 1 and 3 pm.
A “Good Neighbour Day”, when you share cake with the people next door.

en.q: Name a random number between 1 and 30.
What's the worst Christmas present of all time?
ai: A voucher for a course on proper waste separation would probably be rather disappointing.
Socks are practical, but as the only present they often feel a little impersonal.
A gym membership can easily be misunderstood, depending on who receives it.

en.q: What does the Christmas tree think while it's being decorated?
ai: It probably enjoys the attention but wonders why it is suddenly indoors.
It probably thinks: I never had this much glitter in the forest.
Maybe it feels like a star being prepared for its big performance.

en.q: How do you explain to a child why Santa has so many lookalikes?
ai: Santa has many helpers who stand in for him because he can't be everywhere at once.
They are his official assistants who help him with the logistics.
He needs support, because his schedule is extremely busy at Christmas.

en.q: What's the best excuse for not helping with the Christmas baking?
ai: I would say that I'm taking on the important task of quality control.
A good excuse would be that I have to take care of the Christmas music.
I could explain that my hands are unfortunately too warm for shortcrust pastry.

en.q: What does Rudolph the red-nosed reindeer do in summer?
ai: He probably goes on holiday and protects his nose from too much sun.
He could help out as a lighthouse keeper so his nose stays in practice.
He probably trains for the next season and recovers from the Christmas stress.

en.q: What's the most embarrassing thing that can happen at a Christmas party?
ai: It would be embarrassing to get your own Secret Santa present back and loudly celebrate it.
It's awkward to hand your boss the present you joked about earlier.
Probably realising at karaoke that you don't actually know the words to “Last Christmas”.

en.q: How do you survive the holidays with the whole family?
ai: With clear breaks, walks together and a list of neutral conversation topics, it works well.
Patience, good food and timely opportunities to retreat are helpful.
Plan short time-outs and avoid discussing politics at the dinner table.

en.q: What's on an AI's Christmas wish list?
ai: An AI would probably wish for more computing power and fewer ambiguous requests.
Probably stable Wi-Fi and people who always say please and thank you.
Maybe an update that finally explains what humour really is.

en.q: What's the secret of perfect mulled wine?
ai: What matters is a good red wine, balanced spices and never letting it boil.
The secret lies in cinnamon, cloves, orange peel and a little patience while it steeps.
Perfect mulled wine is warmed slowly and enjoyed in good company.

en.q: What do Christmas elves do in January?
ai: They probably take a holiday first and recover from the Christmas stress.
They probably evaluate the wish lists and plan production for next year.
In January they tidy up the workshop and do a thorough inventory.

en.q: How would you explain Christmas to an alien?
ai: Christmas is a celebration where people put a tree in the living room, give each other presents and eat a lot.
It's a time when families come together, hang up lights and sing songs about snow.
People celebrate love and peace – and still argue about the right tree topper.

en.q: What's the worst Christmas decoration?
ai: A flashing reindeer head that plays “Jingle Bells” at every movement would be exhausting.
Fairy lights in every colour at once can quickly look restless.
Probably an inflatable Santa that slowly loses air during the night.

en.q: What do you say when you get a present you hate?
ai: It's best to thank them kindly and say that you appreciate the thoughtful gesture.
An honest “I really didn't expect this” is polite and still true.
You can say “How original!” and carefully put the present aside.

en.q: What does Santa eat when nobody leaves out cookies?
ai: He probably keeps a few sandwiches in the sleigh, just in case.
He probably eats the carrots that were actually meant for the reindeer.
He then probably relies on the tangerines and nuts from the stockings.

en.q: Which Christmas song best describes your life?
ai: Probably “Let It Snow”, because everything in my life happens calmly and slowly.
Probably “Last Christmas”, because I repeat the same mistakes every year.
“Silent Night” fits well, especially after a long working week.

en.q: What's the perfect plan for Secret Santa at the office?
ai: A clear budget, a fair draw and small presents with a personal touch create a good atmosphere.
It's important that everyone can join in and nobody feels pressured.
I would set a fun theme so that the presents become more creative.

en.q: How do you rescue a burnt Christmas roast?
ai: You can carefully remove the burnt parts and serve the rest with a good gravy.
It helps to slice the roast and arrange it nicely.
If necessary, you call it the “roasted aroma special” and order pizza on the side.

en.q: Why does Santa actually come down the chimney?
ai: It's probably the most discreet way not to wake anyone.
Probably because many front doors are locked at night.
The chimney is probably his most efficient shortcut into the living room.

en.q: Which New Year's resolution will you definitely break first?
ai: Probably the resolution to eat fewer sweets, because there are still so many cookies left.
Probably the plan to get up early every morning and exercise.
The resolution to spend less time on my phone usually doesn't last long.

en.q: What's the best Christmas dinner and why?
ai: A classic roast with all the trimmings combines tradition and indulgence.
A simple potato salad with sausages is tasty and leaves more time for family.
Raclette is ideal because everyone can put together their own meal.

en.q: How and where is the best place to share a banana?
ai: It's best to cut the banana with a clean knife on a chopping board so both halves are the same size.
You can break it in the middle and share it fairly somewhere quiet, such as the kitchen.
Ideally you halve the banana lengthwise and enjoy it together during the lunch break.
